                         Entergy Louisiana,            LLC.    (“ELL”   or    the           “Company”) through undersigned counsel,

             respectfully submits this notice that it intends to file an opposition to the Motion for Subpoena for

             the Production of Documents                   (the "'Motion") ﬁled by the Alliance for Affordable Energy and

             Union of Concerned Scientists (collectively. the "'NPOs“) on June 30. 2026, and further requests


             that the Administrative               Hearings Division of the                  Louisiana Public Service Commission    (the

             “LPSC”           or   the   “Commission”) (1) establish a reasonable brieﬁno schedule for the parties to


             respond to the Motion, and (2) schedule a hearing on the Motion to consider the arguments in favor

              of and against the Motion as well as to consider the requests proposed b_v the NPOs for confidential


              information. In further support, the Company asserts as follows:



                         1.        On June 30, 2026, the NPOs filed their Motion seeking ﬁve categories of documents.


                                   each of which is        facially overbroad and seeks discovery of highly commercially

                                   sensitive and confidential materials from                    an   entity not party to this Commission

                                   proceeding.

                           L»)   Rule 40 of the Commissions Rules of Practice and Procedure provides. in part. that



                                 “[n]o    .   .   .   subpoena shall be issued unless the Secretary of the Commission shall

                                 determine that the matter              sought is relevant material         and necessary and that the



                                 production of such books, papers. accounts or documents will not result in unnecessary

                                 harassment, imposition, or undue inconvenience or expense to the party to be required


                                 to produce the same.”



                                 Rule 40 further provides that “[n]o subpoena shall issue for material alleged to be of a


                                 trade secret or conﬁdential nature unless it be shown after hearing of arguments on the


                                 same     that        no   other alternative. such    as   a   protective order. will accomplish a result

                                 consistent with the interests of all parties and the public."


                                 Based on an initial review of the Motion. including the requests identiﬁed by the NPOs


                                 and the arguments asserted in support ofthe Motion_. the NPOs do not appear to have


                                 satisfied the burden imposed               on   them by Rule 40 for issuance of a        subpoena.    ELL



                                 accordingly requests an opportunity to brief the issue of whether the Motion satisﬁes

                                 the requirements for issuance of a subpoena pursuant to the LPSC‘s Rules of Practice


                                 and Procedure.               ELL further asks that the Administrative          Hearings Division set a

                                 hearing to consider arguments made for and against issuance of the proposed subpoena.
